question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The companys latest report, B. which was released only this morning, C. provided the data that D. supports our initial hypothesis
option_2: which was released only this morning
solution_text:
The correct answer is The companys latest report.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word “companys” is incorrect because it shows possession – the report belongs to the company. A possessive singular noun requires an apostrophe before the ‘s’, so it must be written as “company’s”.

• Hence, Part A contains the grammatical error.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Possessive rule: singular noun + ’s (company’s report); plural noun ending in s + apostrophe only (companies’ reports).

• SSC frequently tests apostrophe of possession versus simple plural.

 

NOTE

• Parts B, C and D are grammatically correct – the relative clause, the verb ‘provided’ and the singular verb ‘supports’ (agreeing with ‘data that’) are all properly used.

question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The reason for his failure B. is because he C. didn't study D. for the exam.
solution_text:
The correct answer is is because he.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The construction “The reason is because…” is redundant, since both ‘reason’ and ‘because’ express cause. The correct form is “The reason is that he didn’t study…”.

• Hence, Part B contains the grammatical error.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Rule: use “The reason is that…”, never “The reason is because…”.

• This redundancy error is a favourite in SSC error-spotting questions.

 

NOTE

• Parts A, C and D are correct; only the ‘is because’ portion creates the redundancy error.

question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: SURRENDER
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yield.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ‘Surrender’ means to give up or submit to the control of another. ‘Yield’ also means to give way or give up, making it the closest synonym.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Synonyms of Surrender: yield, submit, capitulate, relinquish, give in.

• Antonyms: resist, defend, withstand.

 

NOTE

• Resist, Confront and Oppose all mean to fight against – they are antonyms of ‘surrender’, not synonyms.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb:

The investigation team will _____ every detail before concluding the report.
solution_text:
The correct answer is go through.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ‘Go through’ means to examine or check something carefully in detail. The team examines every detail, so ‘go through’ fits best.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Go through = examine/scrutinise carefully. Look over = inspect quickly. Call off = cancel. Fall back = retreat/rely on.

 

NOTE

• ‘Look over’ implies a quick glance, not a detailed check; ‘call off’ (cancel) and ‘fall back’ (retreat) do not fit the context of examining details.

question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Diffident
solution_text:
The correct answer is Timid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ‘Diffident’ means lacking self-confidence, shy or timid. Hence ‘Timid’ is the correct synonym.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Synonyms of Diffident: timid, shy, hesitant, reserved, self-doubting.

• Antonyms: confident, bold, assertive.

 

NOTE

• Confident, Bold and Assertive are opposite in meaning to ‘diffident’, so they are antonyms.

question: Choose the correctly spelt word:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Enthusiasm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is “Enthusiasm” (en-thu-si-asm), meaning intense and eager enjoyment or interest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Root: Greek ‘enthousiasmos’ – divine inspiration. Note the ending ‘-asm’, similar to ‘sarcasm’, ‘spasm’.

 

NOTE

• ‘Enthusiarm’, ‘Enthuseam’ and ‘Enthusiasum’ are misspellings and do not exist as valid words.

question:
Which of the following sentences uses the word "bat" with the same meaning as in the following sentence?

"He took a swing with his new wooden bat"
option_1: The bat is the only flying mammal.
option_2: The coach handed him the bat before he went up to the plate.
option_3: A furry little bat got into the attic last night.
option_4: The bat's wingspan was surprisingly large.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The coach handed him the bat before he went up to the plate..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the given sentence, ‘bat’ refers to the wooden implement used to hit a ball in a game. Option 2 (‘the coach handed him the bat before he went up to the plate’) uses ‘bat’ in the same sporting sense.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘Bat’ is a homonym: (i) a sports implement, (ii) a nocturnal flying mammal. Context decides the meaning.

 

NOTE

• Options 1, 3 and 4 use ‘bat’ to mean the flying mammal (mammal, furry, wingspan), a different meaning.

question:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on it:

The mounting reality of climate migration represents a deep and vexing challenge to confront the ethical and planning paradigms of global society. As melting polar ice, desertification, and violent weather patterns make large areas unhabitable, millions are already being forced off their land, in the process creating a new generation of forced migrants who now have no official legal status as "climate refugees." The issue now is no longer whether this will occur, but how countries ought to act together and fairly. A thorough solution calls for a multi-faceted strategy: first, the creation of new international humanitarian and legal protocols to acknowledge and safeguard climate migrants and shift away from the present, limited definition of refugees. Second, it requires proactive, not reactive, policy, such as the establishment of legal and safe channels of resettlement, strong humanitarian assistance for uprooted persons, and serious investment in building climate resilience among those who are likely to be vulnerable, so that they are not displaced in the first place.

It puts in sharp relief the hard question of how the burden is to be shared. A strong case, based on the issue of climate justice, places the main burden on the industrialised world. They have been the biggest per-capita producers of greenhouse gases throughout history, something that is directly associated with the scale of the climate crisis. Their prosperity was primarily developed through carbon-polluting industries, and those are the same conditions responsible for destroying the least-developed countries, which have contributed minimal input to the crisis. Hence, an ethical and equitable response requires that these industrialized countries take the lead with both financial and logistical assistance. They must be leading the line in supporting adaptation projects in developing nations and having the resources necessary for the resettlement and integration of climate migrants. The international community has to eventually realize that the responsibility of climate change is not equally shared, and an equitable solution must involve people who caused the problem taking the initiative to mitigate the most destructive humanitarian effects of the problem.

 

According to the passage, what is the primary ethical dilemma posed by climate migration?
option_1: Whether migrants should be allowed to resettle
option_2: How the burden of climate migration should be shared
option_3: Whether climate change is a natural occurrence
option_4: How to prevent future climate change
solution_text:
The correct answer is How the burden of climate migration should be shared.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage repeatedly stresses “how the burden is to be shared” and how countries “ought to act together and fairly”. The central ethical dilemma is therefore the fair sharing of the burden of climate migration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• In RC, the ‘primary’ idea is the one the whole passage centres on – here, equitable burden-sharing based on climate justice.

 

NOTE

• Options about allowing resettlement, whether climate change is natural, or how to prevent future change are sub-points or unrelated, not the primary ethical dilemma.

In the passage, the word "vexing" most nearly means:

The correct answer is Complex.

What is meant by "climate justice" as described in the passage?
option_2: Accountability of industrialized nations for climate damage
option_4: Global cooperation to reverse climate change
solution_text:
The correct answer is Accountability of industrialized nations for climate damage.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage links ‘climate justice’ to placing “the main burden on the industrialised world” because they have been the biggest producers of greenhouse gases. Thus climate justice means holding industrialized nations accountable for the climate damage they caused.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘Climate justice’ = the idea that those most responsible for emissions should bear the greatest responsibility for remedy.

 

NOTE

• Fair distribution of resources, equity in migration policies, and global cooperation are not how the passage specifically defines climate justice.

How does the passage characterize the current definition of "refugees" in the context of climate migration?
option_1: It is too broad to include climate migrants
option_2: It is narrow and insufficient to cover climate migrants
option_3: It is accurate and universally accepted
option_4: It is too rigid to address global migration
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is narrow and insufficient to cover climate migrants.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage calls for a shift “away from the present, limited definition of refugees” because climate migrants “have no official legal status as ‘climate refugees’”. So the current definition is narrow and insufficient to include them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Keyword ‘limited’ in the passage signals a narrow/insufficient definition.

 

NOTE

• The passage says the definition is limited (narrow), not too broad, not accurate/universally accepted; ‘too rigid to address global migration’ misstates the specific point about climate migrants.

What strategy is suggested in the passage to address climate migration?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Proactive measures to prevent displacement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage explicitly states the response “requires proactive, not reactive, policy” and investment in resilience “so that they are not displaced in the first place”. Hence proactive measures to prevent displacement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Proactive = acting in advance to prevent a problem; Reactive = responding only after it happens.

 

NOTE

• The passage rejects reactive measures, and a total ban or immigration restrictions are never suggested.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: Fallen off the radar
solution_text:
The correct answer is Become unnoticed.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom ‘fallen off the radar’ means to no longer be noticed or receive attention. Hence it means ‘become unnoticed’.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Related: ‘on the radar’ = being noticed/considered; ‘off the radar’ = out of notice/attention.

 

NOTE

• Gained attention and gained popularity are opposites, and ‘avoided detection’ implies deliberate hiding, which is not the idiom’s meaning.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: Dicing with death
solution_text:
The correct answer is Taking extreme risks.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom ‘dicing with death’ means doing something extremely dangerous or taking extreme risks with one’s life. Hence ‘taking extreme risks’.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘Dice with death’ – to engage in a highly risky activity that could be fatal.

 

NOTE

• ‘Playing a dangerous game’ is close but describes an activity rather than the literal risk to life; ‘narrow escape’ and ‘in complete control’ do not convey the idiom’s meaning of extreme risk-taking.

question: Which of the following sentences uses the word "board" with a different meaning from the others?
option_1: The board of directors met yesterday.
option_2: The captain had to board the ship.
option_3: He nailed a picture of the board of directors on the wall.
option_4: The board of directors decided to hire a new CEO.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The captain had to board the ship..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In options 1, 3 and 4, ‘board’ is a noun meaning a group of people (board of directors). In option 2, ‘board’ is a verb meaning to get onto/enter a ship. Hence option 2 differs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘Board’ is a homonym: (i) a governing body, (ii) to get on a vehicle/vessel, (iii) a flat piece of wood.

 

NOTE

• The remaining three sentences all use ‘board’ as the governing body of directors, sharing the same meaning.

question:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A person who loves collecting books.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bibliophile.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A ‘Bibliophile’ is a person who loves and collects books. Hence it is the correct one-word substitute.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Root: Greek ‘biblio’ (book) + ‘phile’ (lover). Compare: bibliophobia (fear of books).

 

NOTE

• A ‘bookworm’ loves reading (not necessarily collecting), a ‘librarian’ manages a library as a job, and a ‘reader’ simply reads.

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Innocuous
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harmful.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ‘Innocuous’ means not harmful or offensive. Its antonym is ‘Harmful’.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Synonyms of Innocuous: harmless, benign, safe, inoffensive. Antonyms: harmful, dangerous, noxious.

 

NOTE

• Harmless, Benign and Safe are synonyms of ‘innocuous’, not antonyms.

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Esoteric
solution_text:
The correct answer is Common.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ‘Esoteric’ means intended for or understood by only a small, specialised group; obscure. Its antonym is ‘Common’, meaning widely known or accessible.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Synonyms of Esoteric: arcane, obscure, mystical, cryptic. Antonyms: common, well-known, familiar.

 

NOTE

• Arcane, Mystical and Obscure are synonyms of ‘esoteric’, not antonyms.

question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

The report could not be accessed without the proper security clearance
option_1: They could not access the report without the proper security clearance.
option_2: The report cannot be accessed without the proper security clearance.
option_3: Without the proper security clearance, the report was not accessed
option_4: The proper security clearance could not access the report.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They could not access the report without the proper security clearance..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passive ‘The report could not be accessed’ becomes active by supplying a logical subject (They) and the base verb: ‘They could not access the report without the proper security clearance.’

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Passive to Active: object of passive becomes object of active, and a suitable subject (they/one) is introduced; ‘could not be accessed’ → ‘could not access’.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 is still passive; option 3 remains passive; option 4 wrongly makes ‘security clearance’ the subject, distorting the meaning.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

The director said, "The new actor will be arriving shortly."
option_1: The director said that the new actor would be arriving shortly.
option_2: The director said that the new actor will be arriving shortly.
option_3: The director said that the new actor would arrive shortly.
option_4: The director said that the new actor had been arriving shortly
solution_text:
The correct answer is The director said that the new actor would be arriving shortly..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In indirect speech, ‘will be arriving’ (future continuous) changes to ‘would be arriving’. Hence the correct sentence is ‘The director said that the new actor would be arriving shortly.’

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Reporting-verb in past tense → will → would; future continuous (will be + -ing) → would be + -ing.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 keeps ‘will’ (no back-shift); option 3 changes the tense form to simple ‘would arrive’ losing the continuous aspect; option 4 wrongly uses ‘had been arriving’.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

Each of the girls narrated their story
option_1: Each of the girls narrated there story
option_2: Each of the girls narrated his story
option_3: Each of the girls narrated her story
option_4: Each of the girls narrated their stories
solution_text:
The correct answer is Each of the girls narrated her story.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ‘Each’ is singular and, since the subject is ‘girls’, the correct singular feminine possessive is ‘her’. Hence ‘Each of the girls narrated her story.’

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Rule: ‘Each of + plural noun’ takes a singular verb and singular pronoun; gender is decided by the noun (girls → her).

 

NOTE

• ‘There’ is a wrong homophone; ‘his’ uses the wrong gender; ‘their stories’ wrongly makes it plural after singular ‘each’.

question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

My brother built this house in 2005.
option_1: This house was built by my brother in 2005.
option_2: This house is built by my brother in 2005.
option_3: This house is built by my brother in 2005.
option_4: This house was being built by my brother in 2005.
solution_text:
The correct answer is This house was built by my brother in 2005..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is in the simple past active (‘built’). Its passive is ‘was/were + past participle’: ‘This house was built by my brother in 2005.’

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Simple past passive = was/were + V3. Object ‘this house’ becomes the subject.

 

NOTE

• Options 2 and 3 use present ‘is built’ (wrong tense); option 4 uses past continuous passive ‘was being built’, which changes the meaning.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.

The professor explained that although the theory had been considered correct for centuries, new findings now proved that it was flawed.
option_1: The professor explained, "Although the theory had been considered correct for centuries, new findings now prove that it is flawed."
option_2: The professor explained, "Although the theory was considered correct for centuries, new findings now prove that it is flawed."
option_3: The professor explained, "Although the theory has been considered correct for centuries, new findings now prove that it is flawed."
option_4: The professor explained, "Although the theory was considered correct for centuries, new findings then proved that it was flawed."
solution_text:
The correct answer is The professor explained, "Although the theory has been considered correct for centuries, new findings now prove that it is flawed.".

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Converting to direct speech reverses the back-shift: ‘had been considered’ → ‘has been considered’, ‘now proved’ → ‘now prove’, and ‘was flawed’ → ‘is flawed’. Option 3 matches all these changes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Indirect to Direct: past perfect → present perfect, past simple → present, and ‘now’ is retained within the quotation.

 

NOTE

• Options 1, 2 and 4 fail to correctly reverse the tenses (retaining ‘had been’/‘was considered’ or ‘then proved…was flawed’).

question:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. The old man, with his kind eyes and twisted hands, smiled softly.

Q. He had lived a whole life as a woodcarver, and his store was a museum of fragile works of art.

R. He held a tiny bird he was carving, his thumb caressing the slippery wood.

S. They all had a story, a memory, a piece of his soul.
solution_text:
The correct answer is PQRS.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• P introduces the old man; Q describes his life as a woodcarver and his store of art; R shows him carving a tiny bird; S concludes that the works all had a story – a piece of his soul. The logical order is P-Q-R-S.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• In para-jumbles, find the opening sentence (introduces the subject – here P) and trace the flow of ideas to the concluding line (S).

 

NOTE

• QPRS, QSRP and SQPR break the logical introduction-to-conclusion flow of the paragraph.

question:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P: She examined the old manuscript closely, observing the fading ink.

Q: After that, she turned the fragile pages carefully so as not to break them any more.

R: With a long history filled with tales, the book has been handed down through the centuries.

S: Before starting the restoration procedure, she got the equipment and supplies she would need ready
solution_text:
The correct answer is R, S, P, Q.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• R introduces the book with its long history; S sets the scene as she gets equipment ready before restoration; P describes her examining the manuscript; Q follows with ‘After that’ as she turns the pages. The order is R-S-P-Q.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Clue words help: ‘Before starting’ (S) precedes the action, and ‘After that’ (Q) must follow the earlier step (P).

 

NOTE

• The other sequences place ‘After that’ (Q) or the introductory line (R) out of order, breaking the logical time sequence.
